newsitem.title: USA: Three Cubans escape Guantanamo base in stolen boat.
newsitem.headline: Three Cubans escape Guantanamo base in stolen boat.

text.p: Three Cuban asylum seekers managed to escape from the sprawling U.S. Naval Base at Guantanamo Bay earlier this month by commandeering a recreational boat, a Navy spokesman said on Wednesday.

The three men, who were being held at the base pending a decision on their appeals for asylum, were working as volunteers at the base marina when they stole a recreational motor boat on Sept. 6, he said. News of their escape only became public this week.

The boat was found dead in the water several days later off the coast of Haiti by a merchant ship. Two of the Cubans jumped off and a third was picked up and remained on the freighter, which another government official said was expected to arrive in Miami sometime in October.

"It has been confirmed that one made it ashore in Haiti, the other is presumed lost at sea," the Navy spokesman said. He said the U.S. State Department was the lead agency in determining the fate of the two survivors, although neither was in U.S. custody Wednesday.

Two of the three Cubans had been repatriated to Cuba after attempting to reach the United States, but sneaked back onto the base. The third had been at Guantanamo awaiting a decision on his immigration status for 11 months.
